name: Hungary: participant-facing document QC
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/hungary/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026); C5.14, C8.08, C9.08 and C9.09 also from the Hungary ICF and minors guides
section_map: C1-C6 = QC sections 1-6; C7 = QC sections 7 (insurance, injury, reimbursement) and 8 (patient emergency card); C8 = QC section 9; C9 = QC section 10; C4.01, C8.09-C8.11 and C10 are the common TrialAgents items.
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: EU clinical trial number, protocol number and trial title are correct and identical across all participant documents.
The Hungarian site and healthcare-provider details match the submitted site package (N1).
Investigator or information-provider names and roles are current.
Study purpose, duration, planned participant numbers, procedures, intervention frequency and visit burden match the protocol.
Accepted alternatives to trial participation are described accurately, including whether joining means interrupting an existing treatment and what that could mean.
Known and reasonably foreseeable risks, burdens and discomforts are consistent with the protocol and current safety information, including the possibility of unforeseen adverse events.
The document says explicitly when no direct participant benefit is expected.
The probability and practical meaning of placebo assignment are explained.
The investigational medicinal product and any necessary plain-language mechanism description are correct.
Contraception, pregnancy testing and pregnancy-reporting wording matches the protocol.
Sample types, volumes, collection times and analyses match the protocol.
Data and sample retention periods match the approved plan.
Reimbursement and travel arrangements match the financial documents (HU-P1).
Emergency contact arrangements match the site information and the patient emergency card.
Every optional substudy in the protocol has a corresponding optional consent pathway where needed.
The protocol contains no participant-facing procedure that is absent from the Hungarian information.
The participant receives the information before signing.
The participant or authorised person has the correct signature and date fields; where a Section 16 Health Act authorised person consents, their identity details are in the consent document.
The principal investigator or person providing the information has the required signature field.
Each separate consent document has one coherent signature set; signature pages are not duplicated.
Optional decisions are separated from mandatory participation decisions.
Withdrawal is described as possible without reason and without disadvantage.
The document explains any lawful consequences of withdrawal, such as handling of data already collected.
Genetic consent is not merged into the main ICF: separate genetic information and consent documents are present.

Every inclusion pathway in the protocol maps to a population, populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage, and each population has its full Hungarian document set (playbook section 2a).
Adults with capacity have the standard Hungarian ICF.
Healthy volunteers have wording suitable for a person with no therapeutic indication and, where relevant, transparent compensation information (healthy-volunteer guide).
Minors have age- and maturity-appropriate information plus the correct parent or legal-representative pathway (minor consent and assent guide); the minor's opinion and dissent handling are explained.
Adults with restricted capacity have participant and representative material appropriate to the legal situation (limited-capacity guide).
Emergency-enrolment trials have a prospectively described later-information and consent pathway (emergency enrolment guide).
If a participant cannot read or write, the form supports Hungary's two-witness oral-consent process (impartial witness guide).
Pregnancy follow-up has separate documents for the participant or pregnant partner where the data subject and consent decision differ (pregnancy follow-up guide).
Optional future use is covered by a separate or clearly separable choice (secondary-use guide).
The sponsor and other controllers or processors are identified as required by the approved privacy model.
The categories of personal and special-category data actually collected are listed, with consistent terminology.
'Coded', 'pseudonymised' and 'anonymous' are used consistently; the same transfer is not described as anonymous in one section and coded in another.
The document explains which parties may access source records and under what conditions (at the site, as described by ETT-KFEB).
The document explains how data leave the site and whether the code key stays at the site.
Recipients or recipient categories are named specifically enough for the participant to understand.
Purpose of processing and the legal basis described in the Hungary-approved wording are stated (ETT-KFEB expects consent; checked against the sponsor's GDPR analysis).
Storage duration and location are stated.
Third-country transfers and their safeguards are explained.
The participant's rights and NAIH contact information are included.
The third-party reimbursement service: exactly which data it receives and why.
A separate pregnant-partner information sheet contains privacy information for the partner.
A substudy with a separate information sheet includes or appropriately cross-references the privacy information for that substudy.
Privacy information is integrated into the participant document; a separate privacy appendix, if used, has its own participant or healthy-volunteer signature field and the main ICF refers to it.
The biological samples taken and the primary study purpose are stated.
Storage duration, location, coding and transfer are stated.
What happens to samples after the primary research purpose ends is stated.
Future use is optional when it is not required for the main study.
For non-anonymous secondary use, the future purpose was explained at the original consent; otherwise renewed consent is planned (ETT-KFEB).
Genetic sampling uses the separate Hungarian genetic information and consent structure with the choices required under the Genetics Act (permitted uses and storage forms).
Withdrawal instructions distinguish identifiable or coded material from material already irreversibly anonymised.

sections.title: Hungary-specific checks: insurance, injury, reimbursement and patient emergency card

items.check: The insurer is named.
The insurer's Hungarian contact details are included.
The contact person's name and telephone number are included.
The document explains whom the participant contacts after trial-related injury.
Treatment and compensation rights are explained in language consistent with Hungarian law (Act XCV of 2005, Section 21).
If reimbursement is offered, the exact documented cost types are listed.
Vague wording such as 'may reimburse' is removed where the sponsor has defined reimbursable costs.
An external reimbursement provider's relationship with the participant and the data flows are explained.
A final Hungarian patient emergency card is included for the trial.
The card has participant name and date-of-birth fields.
The card identifies the protocol and the investigational medicinal product.
The mechanism is added when the product name alone does not explain the relevant safety context.
The card gives indication, contraindications and dangerous interactions.
The card gives the site address and a 24-hour medical contact (investigator or designated physician).
The ICF tells the participant that the card will be issued, what personal data it shows, and to carry it during the trial.
If participant identity and study code appear together on the card, the patient-safety reason is explained and consented in the ICF.
The ETT-KFEB exception for Phase IV and bioequivalence trials was checked before creating or omitting a card; the exception is applied only where the trial genuinely falls within those categories.
Every document has a version number and date consistent with the Hungarian Part II document list (HU-DOC-LIST).
No participant-facing form is pre-signed for CTIS submission.
The main ICF contains participant or authorised-person and investigator or information-provider signature and date fields.
Two witness signature fields plus witness address or contact fields are present where the oral-consent pathway can apply.
Genetic documents each have their own coherent signature set.
Pregnancy-partner documents are signed by the pregnant partner when her data or records are collected.
The Hungarian cover letter and document list identify the same versions.
The consent record contains the participant's name, place of birth and date of birth, and no participant study code number.
Correct CTIS section and naming convention (requirements.json ctis_title, _HU_hu).
No personal data that should not appear in the CTIS upload.

No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] notes, ........... gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/OTHERWISE/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); fields completed at the consent visit stay blank.
Final Hungarian text is used for participant-facing and recruitment material.
The text has been reviewed by a competent Hungarian-language reviewer with clinical-trial knowledge.
Formal address and verb forms are consistent (Ön in adult documents; tegező in child and adolescent documents as the templates set).
Literal English constructions that sound unnatural or change meaning are removed.
Foreign-law references that do not apply in Hungary are removed and replaced by the Hungarian and EU rules that apply.
Medical and regulatory terms are explained understandably.
Headings and consent choices are visually clear.
Terminology is consistent across the main ICF, recruitment materials, emergency card, pregnancy documents, genetic consent and substudy information.
A child-facing document is written for the child, not a literal translation of the adult ICF.
No protocol fact, consent giver, optional choice, data transfer, sample purpose, payment or signature block is unresolved; each resolution is recorded and the affected checks rerun.
